critical_issues.description: Hardcoded file path 'static/index.html' without using os.path.join or pathlib; may fail on Windows or non-standard directory structures.
Hardcoded file path 'static/css/style.css' without using os.path.join or pathlib; may fail on Windows or non-standard directory structures.
Hardcoded file path 'static/js/app.js' without using os.path.join or pathlib; may fail on Windows or non-standard directory structures.
No cleanup of file handle after reading; while context manager is used, the test should verify the file is readable and handle potential UnicodeDecodeError or PermissionError.
No cleanup of file handle after reading; while context manager is used, the test should verify the file is readable and handle potential UnicodeDecodeError or PermissionError.
No cleanup of file handle after reading; while context manager is used, the test should verify the file is readable and handle potential UnicodeDecodeError or PermissionError.
Test uses '/health' but API contract specifies '/api/v1/health'; endpoint mismatch will cause false positives.
Test for '/items' endpoint does not match documented API contract (missing '/api/v1' prefix); likely testing wrong path.
Test for POST '/items' endpoint does not match documented API contract (missing '/api/v1' prefix); likely testing wrong path.
Test for GET '/items/{item_id}' endpoint does not match documented API contract (missing '/api/v1' prefix); likely testing wrong path.
Test hits '/health' but API contract specifies '/api/v1/health' as the health endpoint; mismatch will cause test to fail or test incorrect endpoint.
Test expects response body to be exactly {'status': 'healthy'}, but API contract only specifies 'status' as a string without value constraints; should validate presence and type, not hardcoded value.
Test hits '/' for static files, but frontend documentation shows '/dashboard' as the main page; test should verify '/dashboard' endpoint if it exists, or clarify if '/' is intended.

Test assertion uses '/api/' as a generic pattern, but API contract specifies '/api/v1/health' — this may pass for wrong reasons (e.g., '/api/v2/' or unrelated strings) and does not validate the exact required endpoint.

Test only checks for presence of '/api/items' OR '/api/health', but API contract requires '/api/v1/health'. '/api/health' is not the documented endpoint; this test may pass incorrectly or miss critical mismatches.

Missing import for 'pytest' — test functions should be discoverable by pytest, but no assertions or fixtures use pytest-specific features; however, more importantly, the test file lacks 'pytest' import which is standard practice and may cause issues in strict environments.
Test does not validate the exact value of 'status' field (e.g., 'healthy' or 'ok') as implied by the API contract — only checks it's a string, which is insufficient for verifying correct behavior.

Test for '/dashboard' does not verify that the HTML is valid, accessible, or matches the 'Clean, modern, accessible' design direction; it only checks for static asset paths, which may be brittle and not reflect actual frontend rendering behavior.
Test assumes /health endpoint exists, but API contract specifies /api/v1/health; test uses wrong path.
Test expects response body {"status": "healthy"}, but API contract only specifies {"status": "string"} — test should not assume value beyond type unless explicitly documented.

Module-level mutation of app (app.include_router(router)) causes side effects during import, which violates test isolation and can cause unpredictable behavior when tests run in parallel or when modules are imported multiple times.
Test imports and modifies a global app instance instead of using a fixture to create a fresh app per test, risking state leakage between tests.
Test assumes '/api/v1/flood/predict' endpoint exists, but no corresponding API contract is defined in api_contracts — violates API contract compliance.
Test assumes '/api/v1/flood/history' endpoint exists, but no corresponding API contract is defined in api_contracts — violates API contract compliance.
Missing import for 'Depends' and 'status' from FastAPI; 'status' is needed for proper HTTP status codes (e.g., 201 for POST).

Pydantic models use 'datetime' without timezone awareness; this can cause inconsistencies across timezones and database storage. Should use 'datetime' with 'tzinfo' or 'datetime.datetime' from 'pydantic_extra_types' or enforce UTC.
Database connection is not closed in case of exception (e.g., cursor.execute fails after connection but before conn.close()). Should use try/finally or context manager.
POST endpoint does not return HTTP 201 Created status; it returns default 200 OK, which violates REST conventions for resource creation.
GET /api/inundation endpoint is incomplete (truncated at line 85); missing return statement and exception handling cleanup.
Missing health check endpoint '/api/v1/health' as required by API contracts.

The error display section uses inline style='display: none;' which bypasses CSS variables and makes state management brittle; should be controlled via CSS classes and CSS variables for consistency and theming.
The 'System Health' section lacks a meaningful label for screen readers; the h2 'System Health' is present but the loading state has no accessible name or role to indicate its purpose during loading.
The 'Live Flood Data' section has no aria-live region or dynamic update indication, making real-time data updates inaccessible to assistive technologies.

The 'Evacuation Router' section is critical safety functionality but has no visual or semantic indication of urgency or priority (e.g., no role='alert' or high-priority styling), risking user confusion during emergencies.
Incomplete CSS rule: '.text-center' declaration block is missing closing brace and content, causing CSS parse failure and breaking subsequent styles.
File starts with invalid syntax: triple-quoted string literal (Python-style) instead of JavaScript comment or code. This will cause immediate parse failure in browsers.

DOM object contains over 100 properties, many of which appear to be unused or redundant (e.g., 20+ evacuationMap* handlers), indicating poor maintainability and potential memory leaks from orphaned event handlers.
File is incomplete (truncated mid-identifier), making it non-functional and causing syntax errors.

moderate_issues.description: String search for 'dashboard' and 'flood' is case-insensitive but not robust (e.g., substring matches like 'dashboarding' or 'floodwater' may yield false positives); consider using regex or more precise checks.

Whitespace-insensitive 'fetch(' check is implemented inefficiently via string replacement instead of using regex or simpler normalization (e.g., 'fetch(' in content.replace(' ', '').replace('\n', '')).
Only os is imported; using pathlib.Path would improve cross-platform path handling and readability.
Using MagicMock() without specifying return_value or side_effect may lead to tests that pass incorrectly; consider using spec or spec_set to enforce stricter mocking.
Same as above — Redis client mock lacks spec/spec_set, risking over-mocking and false positives.
Test for 404 case uses ValueError exception, but FastAPI typically raises HTTPException or custom exceptions; behavior may not match production.
Assertion for 404 response detail message is fragile: checks both 'not found' and 'Item not found' — should rely on consistent error format from the app.
Test assumes 'content-type' header exists and is accessible; should use response.headers.get('content-type') to avoid KeyError if header is missing.
Test checks for substring in response.text without verifying it's non-empty or valid HTML; could mask rendering issues or changes in branding.

Test for exports/functions is overly permissive — matching 'const ' or 'let ' could match arbitrary code (e.g., comments, strings), not necessarily actual function definitions. Should validate actual function declarations or exports more precisely.
No test verifies that the correct HTTP method (GET) is used with the endpoint — only presence of the URL string is checked, not fetch() usage with method: 'GET'.
Direct import of 'app' from 'src.main' may cause side effects at module import time (e.g., DB connections, config loading) — better to use a fixture to lazily instantiate the app.

Test for '/static/index.html' assumes static files are served at that path, but FastAPI does not serve static files at '/static/index.html' by default unless explicitly configured — this may be a false positive or misconfiguration.

Test `test_css_file_contains_css_variables` uses overly loose matching: `:root` or `var(` may appear in comments or unrelated contexts, leading to false positives. A more robust check (e.g., regex for actual variable definitions like `--var-name:`) is recommended.

Test `test_css_file_contains_expected_design_system_properties` checks for substring presence (e.g., 'color') which may match inside comments or strings (e.g., '/* color palette */'), causing false positives. Consider using regex with word boundaries or property declarations.
Basic brace/parentheses balancing checks do not account for nested structures, comments, or escaped characters (e.g., in URLs or strings), potentially flagging valid CSS as invalid.
test_app_includes_router mocks api_router but then inspects app.routes — mocking is unnecessary and misleading; the test should either patch app.include_router or avoid mocking entirely.

Route path inspection assumes '/api' substring is sufficient to confirm router inclusion; fragile if router paths change (e.g., /api/v1/health). Should check for specific expected paths like '/api/v1/health'.
test_health_endpoint patches api_router unnecessarily and may interfere with app state; patching should be avoided unless mocking external dependencies.
Payload uses ISO 8601 timestamp string; no validation ensures it's parsed correctly by the endpoint (e.g., pydantic datetime parsing).
Validation error test only checks status code 422; should also validate response body structure (e.g., error detail) to ensure robust error handling.
History endpoint test does not verify pagination, sorting, or filtering behavior if supported by the API contract.
DEBUG is set based solely on ENV == 'development', which may expose sensitive behavior in non-development environments if APP_ENV is misconfigured.
DATABASE_URL default uses sqlite:///app.db, which is insecure for production and may lead to data exposure or loss if deployed without explicit override.
REDIS_URL default assumes localhost availability; in containerized or distributed deployments this may cause connection failures.

ML_MODEL_PATH uses a hardcoded relative path component ('models/model.pt') in the default, but BASE_DIR is resolved from __file__ — this may cause path mismatches if the module is imported from unexpected locations (e.g., tests, entrypoints).
Missing import for 'logging' module; production code should log errors instead of embedding raw exception strings in HTTP details.
Database path uses environment variable fallback without validation; could lead to accidental in-memory or wrong-path DB usage.

Raw SQL queries are vulnerable to SQL injection if input validation is bypassed; although parameters are currently bound, no explicit validation of string fields (e.g., sensor_id) against injection patterns.
Timestamp conversion to ISO string may fail if Pydantic datetime has timezone info inconsistent with SQLite expectations (SQLite stores text as-is); should normalize to UTC before storage.
Missing rate limiting or request throttling for database-heavy endpoints, which could cause performance issues under load.
Logger level is set to INFO unconditionally, which may be too verbose for production or too sparse for debugging; should be configurable via environment variable or parameter.

Handler is added only if no handlers exist, but formatter is not preserved if handlers already exist — could lead to inconsistent logging format across modules if logger is reused with pre-existing handlers.
Google Fonts are loaded with 'display=swap' but no fallback font stack is defined in CSS, risking layout shift or invisible text during load if fonts fail.
The error section uses id='error-display' but no mechanism is defined to ensure it's hidden by default via CSS (e.g., no .hidden class or CSS rule), risking accidental visibility on initial load.
The 'status-loading' text is not marked with role='status' or aria-busy='true' on the parent container, reducing screen reader responsiveness.
The 'data-loading' text lacks a live region attribute (e.g., role='status' or aria-live='polite') to announce updates when real-time data arrives.
The footer links lack aria-labels or context (e.g., 'API Health endpoint' vs 'Documentation'), which is important for screen reader users navigating via links.
Primary color (#1e6f8c) has insufficient contrast ratio (4.46:1) against white background for normal text per WCAG AA; should be ≥4.5:1 for small text or ≥3:1 for large text.
Primary dark color (#15566d) has insufficient contrast ratio (4.35:1) against white background for normal text per WCAG AA; should be ≥4.5:1.
Flood risk colors use identical hex values for low risk (#28a745) and success color, potentially causing confusion between functional states and flood-specific semantics; consider distinct hues.

Using 'display: flex; flex-direction: column;' on body may interfere with legacy browser compatibility and could cause unexpected layout behavior in some contexts; consider using a dedicated wrapper for layout.
Focus ring uses hardcoded primary color value instead of CSS variable (--color-primary), reducing maintainability and theme consistency.
API_BASE is hardcoded as a string literal; should be configurable via environment variable or config object for flexibility across environments (dev/staging/prod).
DOM object uses null initializations without type safety or validation; should use a factory function or class to ensure consistent initialization and avoid runtime null reference errors.
No error handling, loading states, or retry logic for API calls (e.g., missing fetch() calls despite dashboard requiring GET /api/v1/health).
No DOMContentLoaded or window load event listener to ensure DOM elements are available before accessing them.

suggestions: Use pathlib.Path for path handling to improve cross-platform compatibility and code clarity.
Add error handling (e.g., FileNotFoundError, UnicodeDecodeError) around file operations.
Parameterize file paths using fixtures or constants to avoid duplication and improve maintainability.
Replace substring checks with more robust assertions (e.g., regex, DOM parsing if HTML, or AST for JS).
Consider using pytest's tmp_path or temporary directory fixtures for isolation if tests ever need to write files.
Add type hints to function signatures for better IDE and static analysis support.
Add type hints to fixture return types (e.g., -> MagicMock) for better IDE and type checker support.
Consider using `spec` or `spec_set` in MagicMock() to prevent accidental attribute access in tests (e.g., MagicMock(spec_set=['execute', 'commit']) for DB mock).
If real database or Redis behavior is partially emulated, consider using `MagicMock(spec=...)` with actual client classes (e.g., `spec=redis.Redis`) if available.
Document expected methods/attributes that tests will call on the mocks to improve maintainability.
Update all endpoint paths to include '/api/v1' prefix to match API contracts.
Ensure the router under test actually registers routes with the documented paths.
Replace ValueError with HTTPException or a custom exception that matches production error handling.
Standardize error detail message assertions to match the app's actual error response format (e.g., using 'detail' key consistently).
Add tests for missing required fields in request payloads beyond just empty dict (e.g., missing 'name' field).
Add tests for other documented endpoints not covered (e.g., PUT/DELETE if applicable).
Use Pydantic models in mocks to ensure request/response validation matches production behavior.
Consider adding integration tests that verify actual route registration and response structure.
Add tests for the correct API endpoint path '/api/v1/health' as per contract.
Use response.json() validation with partial matching (e.g., assert response.json()['status'] == 'healthy' or isinstance(response.json()['status'], str)).
Add test for '/dashboard' if it's a static page endpoint, or clarify if '/' is the intended root.
Consider parameterizing health endpoint tests to avoid duplication.
Add type hints to test functions for better IDE and mypy support.
Use fixtures for TestClient to avoid repeated instantiation and improve test performance.
Update endpoint assertions to strictly match '/api/v1/health' as per API contract.
Add test to verify fetch() calls include method: 'GET' for health endpoint.
Use regex or AST-based parsing (e.g., with `esprima` or `acorn` via subprocess) for more robust JS structure validation instead of string substring matching.
Consider mocking or isolating file system access in tests to avoid side effects during CI runs.
Add test for absence of deprecated or incorrect endpoints (e.g., ensure '/api/items' is not present if not in contract).
Include error handling in test for file read failures (e.g., encoding issues).
Add a pytest fixture to manage TestClient lifecycle and app initialization to avoid side effects.
Use parameterized tests or fixtures to validate response schemas with Pydantic models where possible.
Consider using HTML parsing (e.g., BeautifulSoup) instead of string matching for HTML assertions to improve robustness.
Add assertions for response headers (e.g., Content-Type) to ensure correct content negotiation.
Include tests for error cases (e.g., 5xx responses, invalid inputs) to improve coverage.
Add type hints to test functions and variables for better maintainability.
Add a `pytest.mark.parametrize` or use a CSS parser (e.g., `cssutils`) for more accurate syntax validation instead of manual counting.
Consider making `css_file_path` configurable via environment variable or CLI option for flexibility in CI/CD environments.
Add type hints to fixture and test functions for better IDE and static analysis support.
Include a test for CSS file encoding (e.g., UTF-8) to prevent encoding-related issues in production.
Add a test to verify that critical design system variables (e.g., `--primary-color`) are defined, aligning with the frontend's design system requirements.
Update test_health_endpoint to use '/api/v1/health' per API contract.
Remove unnecessary mocking in test_health_endpoint and test_app_includes_router.
Add explicit test for /api/v1/health endpoint with correct path and response structure.
Consider parameterizing health endpoint tests to cover both /health (if legacy) and /api/v1/health.
Add tests for error responses (e.g., 5xx) if applicable.
Ensure src/main.py exports only intended public symbols (e.g., via __all__) to avoid accidental coupling in tests.
Use a pytest fixture to create a fresh FastAPI app instance per test (e.g., @pytest.fixture def app(): ... app.include_router(router); yield app) to avoid module-level side effects.
Add API contract definitions for '/api/v1/flood/predict' and '/api/v1/flood/history' to ensure test coverage aligns with documented interfaces.
Include type hints for request/response models in tests (e.g., using Pydantic models) to improve maintainability and catch mismatches early.
Add negative test cases for invalid input types (e.g., string for rainfall_mm) and boundary values (e.g., negative rainfall).
Consider parameterizing tests for multiple valid/invalid payloads to increase coverage and reduce duplication.
Add cleanup or mocking for history endpoints if they rely on persistent state (e.g., database), to ensure idempotent test runs.
Add validation for required environment variables (e.g., DATABASE_URL in production) and raise explicit errors if missing.
Use pydantic or similar for structured config validation to enforce types and provide better error messages.
Consider separating config loading logic (e.g., into a function) to avoid side effects at import time.
Add type hints for all config variables (e.g., API_PORT: int).
Add a production-specific check that prevents DEBUG=True in non-development environments.
Use pathlib operations consistently (e.g., BASE_DIR / 'models' / 'model.pt' instead of str(...) in default).
Use FastAPI's Depends() for database connection management to ensure proper cleanup and testability.
Add Pydantic model validation for location strings (e.g., regex for valid coordinate-like or named locations).
Implement database schema versioning/migrations to avoid runtime errors from missing tables.
Replace raw dict(row) conversion with explicit model parsing (e.g., SensorData(**row)) to enforce type safety and schema alignment.
Add input sanitization for string fields (e.g., strip whitespace, limit length) before DB insertion.
Consider using async database drivers (e.g., asyncpg, aiosqlite) for better scalability.
Add request/response logging middleware for auditability in production.
Define and use HTTPException subclasses for domain-specific errors (e.g., DatabaseUnavailable, InvalidInput).
Add support for configurable log level (e.g., via environment variable or optional parameter).
Consider using `logging.NullHandler` as fallback for library modules to avoid 'No handlers could be found' warnings.
Add `__name__ == '__main__'` guard if this module is ever run directly for testing.
Use `logging.basicConfig()` or a more robust configuration pattern (e.g., dictConfig) for production deployments.
Add type hints for return value (already present) and consider using `logging.LoggerAdapter` for structured logging support.
Replace all aria-busy attributes with dynamic role='status' or role='alert' as appropriate for urgency.
Define CSS custom properties (e.g., --color-critical, --font-heading) in style.css and ensure all text meets WCAG AA contrast ratios.
Add a 'last updated' timestamp or refresh indicator for real-time data sections.
Ensure app.js implements proper error handling with user-friendly messages and retries for health/flood data endpoints.
Consider adding a skip-to-content link for keyboard accessibility.
Add a meta description tag for SEO and accessibility context.
Replace placeholder 'Loading...' text with more descriptive, context-aware messages (e.g., 'Connecting to sensor network...').
Ensure evacuation router section has visual priority cues (e.g., border color, icon) and is focusable/announced as high-priority.
Add missing closing brace for .text-center rule and implement actual centering styles (e.g., text-align: center).
Increase primary color contrast by darkening to #164e63 or similar to meet WCAG AA (≥4.5:1).
Add a dark theme variant using prefers-color-scheme media query for improved accessibility in low-light conditions.
Include focus-visible polyfill fallback for browsers without :focus-visible support.
Add responsive typography using clamp() for base font size to improve mobile readability.
Define semantic color aliases (e.g., --color-text-primary) to decouple text colors from semantic meanings.
Add missing utility classes (e.g., .d-flex, .flex-row, .m-auto) commonly needed for responsive layouts.
Consider adding a CSS reset for form elements to ensure consistent appearance across browsers.
Replace the malformed string prefix with a proper JSDoc-style comment block.
Refactor DOM references into a dedicated initialization function that caches elements once and validates existence.
Implement proper async/await fetch logic for /api/v1/health with error states and last-updated timestamp updates.
Remove unused evacuationMap* properties (e.g., handlers, offsets, states) unless actively used in current feature scope.
Add accessibility attributes (aria-live, role, focusable) to status card and loading/error elements.
Define and use CSS custom properties (e.g., --color-status-ok, --font-heading) in style.css to support the Nunito + Crimson Pro typography and design checklist.
Add a config module (e.g., config.js) to centralize API endpoints, feature flags, and environment-specific values.
Implement cleanup logic (e.g., removeEventListeners) to prevent memory leaks when components re-render or unmount.
Add unit tests for core functions (e.g., fetchHealthStatus, updateStatusUI).
Ensure all UI text is localized or at least uses meaningful static labels (no 'Loading...' placeholders).
